disclaimer: Personal portfolio demo on synthetic data. Not financial, pricing or legal advice. The tool shows evidence and risk from past matters; a person decides the price.

inputs.cost_rates_note: PLACEHOLDER values for the demo only. Internal cost per hour by level is an input that finance must supply; these figures are invented and are not estimates of any firm's costs.
inputs.mapping: Synthetic export, shape A (four tidy files)

rules: Closed before 2026-01-01 (open matters are never comps).
Matters that closed abnormally (settled early, transferred, other) are excluded.
At least 8 comps are required before any figure is shown.

backtest.scope: Out of sample. Walk-forward back-test of every closed internal_investigation matter, each modeled only from matters that closed before it opened, with the change check and the band adjustment also run as of that day. Matched on matter type only (not this proposal's selection rules), minimum 8 comps.
backtest.headline: Overruns at P75 and P90 are within what chance would explain at n=31.
backtest.verdict: Overruns at P75 and P90 are within what chance would explain at n=31. At the planning P75, 10 of 31 back-tested matters cost more; the band implies about 8. At the planning P90, 5 of 31 back-tested matters cost more; the band implies about 3. Costs appear to have risen: the 26 matters opened from 2022-04-12 cost 1.78x the 15 opened before, at the same rates. A prompt to look, not a finding. Each planning band is the higher of the recent-only and whole-history versions, so the flag can raise a band but not lower it.

distribution.basis: Normalized value: hours worked x the 2026 rate card, after any hours-reduction assumptions.

ai.label: User assumptions, not predictions. The tool does not estimate any effect of AI on hours.

notes: Adjusted from 31 earlier matters of this type whose outcome against their own bands is known. Raised: P25 x1.10, P50 x1.30, P75 x1.41, P90 x1.57.
Change check: every band taken from the recent-only version because it is higher.
planning.label: Planning figures

scenarios.label: Fixed fee $100,000
notes: Revenue is the fee on every comp, whatever the work turned out to be.
scenarios.in_sample_note: In sample: counted on the same comps the bands were built from.

out_of_sample.where: Fee is between the planning P25 ($73,500) and P50 ($125,000).
out_of_sample.text: Fee is between the planning P25 ($73,500) and P50 ($125,000). Walk-forward, back-tested matters of this type: 10 of 31 at or under their planning P25 (the band implies 25%); 16 of 31 at or under their planning P50 (the band implies 50%).

scenarios.label: Capped fee, cap $130,000
notes: Billed hourly at standard rates up to the cap; work above the cap is not paid.
scenarios.in_sample_note: In sample: counted on the same comps the bands were built from.

out_of_sample.where: Fee is between the planning P50 ($125,000) and P75 ($199,500).
out_of_sample.text: Fee is between the planning P50 ($125,000) and P75 ($199,500). Walk-forward, back-tested matters of this type: 16 of 31 at or under their planning P50 (the band implies 50%); 21 of 31 at or under their planning P75 (the band implies 75%).

assumptions.text: The 10 comps above the P75 cost $122,100 more on average than the other 31. Discovery and diligence accounts for 51% of that gap ($61,900). Set a scope limit or a separate fee for that phase.

4 matters of this type closed abnormally (settled early, transferred or other) and are not in the comps. The figures assume the matter runs to completion; say what happens to the fee if it ends early.
The phase split for 5 of 41 comps comes from the date-window fallback, not task codes. Treat per-phase figures as lower confidence; totals are not affected.

Across the 41 comps, 5.3% of worked value was written down before billing and 3.8% of invoiced fees was not collected. A fee built from billed amounts would understate the work; the figures here use worked hours.

Costs for this matter type appear to have risen: the 26 matters opened from 2022-04-12 cost 1.78x the 15 opened before, at the same rates (medians $96,800 and $54,300). The date is estimated from the data, and the check is a prompt to look, not a finding. A flag can only raise a planning figure: each one is the higher of the recent-only and whole-history versions.
